description:
Reverse lookup across a small CIDR range: which hostnames have been observed on any address in it. NEEDS AN API KEY ON THE PLUS PLAN OR ABOVE.

THE RANGE IS CAPPED AT 256 ADDRESSES: an IPv4 /24 or narrower. Ask for /24s, and issue several calls rather than one wide one; a wider range is refused with a message, not truncated. For a single address use domains_on_ip. Paging works as in domains_on_ip: after="" starts a stable walk, then pass next_cursor back.

The same caution as domains_on_ip applies more strongly here: names sharing a /24 usually share a hosting provider and nothing else.

after.description: Paging. Send an EMPTY string to start a stable walk in key order, then pass each reply's next_cursor back here. Omit it for the most recently seen names first, which cannot be paged.

cidr.description: A CIDR range covering at most 256 addresses, e.g. "8.8.8.0/24" or a narrower prefix. For one address use domains_on_ip.

first_seen_from.description: Only hostnames FIRST observed at this address at or after this time. RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. It narrows the answer, not the work: use it to cut the number of pages.

first_seen_to.description: Only hostnames first observed at or before this time, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Pair with first_seen_from to isolate a provisioning window; either may be given alone.

limit.description: Maximum hostnames to return. Default 500, maximum 50000; larger values are capped.

name: domains_in_range

next_cursor.description: Present when another page exists. Pass it as after.

order.description: recent (last seen first, not pageable) or key (stable; page with next_cursor).

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the result short.

title: Domains in an address range
